No.29

May Eggs and Milk Be Eaten?

On choices of food and daily goods, the author's question about purity and convenience.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva: may vegetarians eat eggs and milk? Is it wrong to use leather goods?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"The purity of food
lies chiefly in the heart."
"Not for the sake of taste,
not at the cost of a life,
one may follow conditions."
"If for convenience,
milk and eggs are no sin;
if one seeks purity,
one may also keep away from them."

"In the use of things,
look at their causes;
if the heart holds no cruelty,
using them is no fault."

🔶Plain Rendering

"The purity of food lies chiefly in the heart." Whether food is pure depends on your intention, not only on the food itself. "Not for craving of taste, not harming a life, one may follow conditions." What is not eaten out of greed for flavor and does not harm a life may be eaten as circumstances allow. "If for convenience, milk and eggs are no sin; if one seeks purity, one may also keep away from them."

If it is for the convenience of daily life, eating eggs and milk does not create wrongdoing; if you seek a higher purity, choosing to avoid them is also good.

"In the use of things, look at their causes; if the heart holds no cruelty, using them is no fault."

When using anything, look at the causes behind it — if your heart holds no intention to harm, using it is not a fault.
